text:
Alex M.: FYI customer 'acme-prod' opened a support ticket — their Private VPC deployment is losing outbound UDP to their metrics collector, causing many retries and 502s in our agent. Can sec team weigh in?
Maria S.: repro steps / logs? what ports/protocols exact?
Alex M.: Steps from customer:
1) Pod sends statsd over UDP to 10.0.5.7:8125
2) Agent proxies and we see 'connection reset' -> app-level 502
They attached tcpdump showing UDP SYN-like flows (yes, odd wording from customer). Snippet from kube node tcpdump:
---
16:23:11.123456 IP 10.0.1.45.54321 > 10.0.5.7.8125: UDP, length 42
16:23:11.123789 IP 10.0.5.7.8125 > 10.0.1.45.54321: UDP, length 0
---
Packet shows outbound then immediate silence.
Owen T.: sounds like stateful firewall/NAT dropping 'responses' because of asymmetric routing or conntrack timeout. UDP is tricky — if our NAT device isn't keeping conntrack for the ephemeral port mapping, replies get dropped. Does customer sit behind a NAT gateway we manage or their own?
Alex M.: It's their Private deployment (control plane managed by us, dataplane in customer VPC). Their NAT is their provider NAT gateway, but they also have a managed proxy appliance we route through for egress.
Jessica (sec): Also need to confirm KMS/HSM egress isn't affected. If egress rules are too strict and block high-numbered ports, the dataplane might be failing to reach KMS endpoints for key unwrap, causing agent fallback errors that look like 502s. Do we have audit logs showing KMS handshake failures?
Alex M.: Customer reported only metrics affected; their logs show 'agent: proxy: upstream unreachable' repeated. No explicit KMS errors in app logs.
Maria S.: Can we get a packet capture on the proxy egress interface? Also paste the customer's iptables rules and AWS SGs if possible. Quick check: does our proxy do DNAT to a pool and change source port? That would break client expectations if conntrack isn't updated.
Owen T.: If the proxy translates source ports, make sure it's preserving the 5-tuple or tracking replies. Proposed quick checks:
- On proxy: sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 udp and host 10.0.5.7
- On node: sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 udp and host 10.0.5.7
- Check conntrack: sudo conntrack -L | grep 10.0.5.7
Alex M.: forwarding the tcpdumps now. attaching minimal debug from proxy:
---
root@proxy:~# ss -u -n -a | grep 8125
UNCONN     0      0          0.0.0.0:8125       0.0.0.0:*
root@proxy:~# sudo conntrack -L | grep 10.0.5.7
udp      17 src=10.0.1.45 dst=10.0.5.7 sport=54321 dport=8125 src=10.0.0.10 dst=54.23.12.7 sport=40000 dport=8125 [ASSURED] use=1
---
Owen T.: The conntrack entry shows DNAT to 54.23.12.7 (egress proxy pool). Looks normal and is ASSURED. But note the response packet in the earlier tcpdump had length 0 — possibly an ICMP unreachable or filtered. Can we confirm ICMP 'fragmentation needed' or TTL expired?
Maria S.: Customer's security posture team also limits ICMP. If ICMP is blocked, PMTU issues may cause weirdness but not for small UDP packets.
Jessica (sec): From compliance side, two asks: (1) Audit logs: ensure we have VPC Flow Logs / agent audit logs retained per their contract (they requested 90d retention). We currently retain 30d by default for Private — need policy exception? (2) KMS key usage: confirm HSM calls for agent key unwrap show success — if not, egress to kms.<region>.redwood-keysvc must be allowed.
Alex M.: Customer contract says 90d. I checked our console: private deployment audit retention toggle is 30d by default. Escalating.
incident-bot: New escalation INC-2026 created: private-vpc-egress-udp-metrics-block. Priority P2.
oncall-sre: @oncall-sre stepping in to help with repro. Quick test we can run from our infra:
- kubectl run -i --tty tester --image=appropriate/nc --rm -- sh
- echo "ping" | nc -u -w1 10.0.5.7 8125 && echo success || echo fail
If we see immediate failure from inside their network, it's path-level.
Owen T.: If test fails, try forcing source port to a low-value so NAT behavior changes: nc -u -p 40000 10.0.5.7 8125. Also test tcp to same port to distinguish firewall by protocol.
Maria S.: Also need to verify our egress firewall allowlist: currently we allow outbound TCP to KMS endpoints on 443, and allow outbound to statsd IP ranges? We don't have generic UDP allowlist for customer-managed destinations — we usually recommend customer open destination ports for known telemetry endpoints.
Jessica (sec): For the security review: recommend adding to runbook:
- Document expected egress ports (UDP 8125, 1194, etc) per customer app needs
- For Private deployments, require explicit SG rule allowing ephemeral response ports or document that NAT must preserve ephemeral ranges
- Audit retention update request to compliance (90d for this customer)
- Verify HSM/KMS egress endpoints are reachable and logged
Alex M.: Next actions: 1) run nc tests from inside cluster (oncall-sre) 2) collect proxy tcpdump + conntrack (customer provided) 3) open compliance PR to extend audit retention to 90d for acme-prod 4) if confirmed NAT asymmetry, suggest adding UDP destination to our approved egress policy and help customer add SG rules.
Maria S.: I'll draft the firewall change template for the customer to apply (SG rule example + conntrack-check commands).
Owen T.: If we need a quick mitigation, we can enable an agent-side UDP->TCP relay for statsd for a temporary workaround (adds latency but reliable). Ping me if we need to prepare a small sidecar image.
Alex M.: Thanks all — I'll update INC-2026 with the captures and the next steps. Will follow up once we have nc results. :thumbsup:
Jessica (sec): tagging for compliance: please cc me on the PR for audit retention. Also note: any change to egress allowlist requires documented justification + reviewer sign-off per policy.
oncall-sre: ran tests at 16:40 UTC — initial nc UDP test failed, TCP to same port succeeded. Uploading raw captures to the incident thread.
Alex M.: received — moving to triage.
